scope: The four-point divider at a fixed modern 2:1 setting. The screw clamps the pivot. The instrument opens and closes by hand. Thread adjustment is fixed during the demonstration.

sheet_vs_reconstruction: [manifest] Two crossed pointed legs and a screw detail appear with geometrical diagrams.
[geometry] The 0.4 m and0.2 m pivot distances, iron sections and opening schedule are original modern assumptions. No public museum model has been copied.

[geometry] The instrument is built the way a maker of about 1500 would forge and file it: flat legs that swell toward a slot and taper to steeled points, one bolt through both slots with a washer between the legs, and a wing nut in front that clamps the pivot where it is set. The slot, the points, the washers and the wing nut are not on the sheet.
